thread:
maria: Quick question — a few new hires joined mid-pay-period and elected HSA pretax and 401(k) pretax. Payroll put them in as post-tax HSA by mistake for the Apr 14 payday. How do we correct with BrightHealthSavings and avoid 401(k) deferral issues?

liz_hr: Ugh. Are the amounts small or full elections? Do we have employee consent forms verifying pretax election?

maria: Full elective amounts per offer letters. I double-checked elections on the portal. Looks like payroll mapping used WRONG_HSA_CODE.

pete_payroll: Thanks for flagging. If the deduction was processed post-tax we need to do two things: 1) forward-correct the payroll deduction type for the affected paydate and 2) submit an adjustment file to BrightHealthSavings with the original pay date flagged. We can issue a correcting payroll on Apr 21 off-cycle or do it as a retro adjustment on the next regular run. Which do you prefer?

kevin-records: From the recordkeeper side BrightHealthSavings accepts retro remits labeled "ADJ_RETRO". As long as the correction file includes employee DOB/SSN and original pay date, we can reclassify the contribution as pretax for compliance purposes. Try to remit within 5 business days to minimize reporting issues.

maria: We prefer not to run off-cycle unless absolutely needed. If we do retro on next run, employees will see the pre-tax amount netted on their May 1 paystub — is that okay? Will any tax withholdings need manual change?

pete_payroll: If you do retro on next run we can adjust YTD taxable wages and withholdings so W-2s remain correct. Payroll will need a brief memo from People Ops authorizing the change.

liz_hr: I'll draft an authorization note and collect e-signatures (quick Slack approvals fine) from the affected employees. Also need to confirm whether any ER contribution limits (employee + employer) are impacted for catch-up eligibile folks.

maria: Good point — one of these folks is 50+ and electing catch-up HSA. How do we reflect catch-up contributions?

kevin-records: BrightHealthSavings requires catch-up to be flagged in the remittance file with code "CATCHUP_50" per employee. If the catch-up wasn't remitted on Apr 14, include it in the adjustment file and mark the total employee contribution for the calendar year. We reconcile to plan limits monthly.

pete_payroll: For 401(k) there's an extra wrinkle: if the HSA was misclassified post-tax, that doesn't affect 401(k) deferrals, but if payroll mapping was broadly off we should confirm 401k codes. Our deduction map: ```CSV
code,description
HSA_PRE,HSA pretax
HSA_POST,HSA post-tax
401K_PRE,401(k) pretax
401K_ROTH,Roth 401(k)
```

maria: I ran a quick query and only HSA codes were wrong. 401k deductions look correct in the Apr 14 file.

liz_hr: OK — plan: 1) I will collect Slack approvals from employees by EOD 2) Payroll to prepare an "ADJ_RETRO" remittance to BrightHealthSavings with the original pay date 3) Payroll to update internal mapping to prevent recurrence 4) People Ops to send short comms about paystub timing.

oncall-bot: Reminder: create an incident ticket for payroll adj so finance audit trail retains docs. Ticket #INC-4721 created.

pete_payroll: I'll queue the adjustment and aim to remit tomorrow. Will attach the ADJ_RETRO file and the employee approval memo.

kevin-records: We got the file and will process as pretax. Expect updated participant statements within 48 hours and we'll send an email confirmation to payroll and People Ops when posted.

maria: Huge thanks all. Also, can we add a quick validation step to the offer-to-payroll handoff checklist to catch HSA code mismatch? Small change could save a lot.

pete_payroll: Agreed. I'll add a checkbox and a sample CSV to the onboarding playbook.
